newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary KDNP party head quits parliamentary group.
newsitem.headline: Hungary KDNP party head quits parliamentary group.

text.p: The leader of the Hungarian Christian Democratic Party (KDNP) quit its parliamentary group after it ousted three MPs following the decision of the European Union of Christian Democrats (EUCD) to expel the KDNP.
"(Party leader) Gyorgy Giczy has decided to quit the group," Miklos Hasznos, one of the expelled MPs, told journalists on Tuesday after a party disciplinary hearing at which Giczy was not present.

The KDNP announced on Monday the EUCD had expelled it for failing to end internal divisions and sever all ties with Hungary's extreme right, and for not seeking co-operation with centre-right parties.
"The three excluded MPs were mainly responsible for the party's ousting from the EUCD," said Bela Csepe, deputy leader of the KDNP's parliamentary group.

The KDNP has been plagued by internal strife since the right-leaning Giczy became president of the party soon after the 1994 elections. Last week some centrist members formed a separate faction within the party.
The KDNP has 23 seats in the 386-seat Hungarian parliament where a coalition between Socialists and the liberal Free Democrats has 72 percent of the seats.
